g.text: Open or focus a window: mycelium.OpenVSCode(path) / OpenGhostty(tty, path)

Two layers in dashkit/mycelium: Ghostty's own AppleScript surfaces first, System Events window titles second (VS Code: titles only). Callers: canopy (jump to the selected agent's window), understory (Enter on a worktree row), coppice (read-only twin).
Jump to the window that runs the selected agent.
Enter on a worktree row: OpenGhostty("", worktree path). No tty to prefer, so matching is path-only.
Python twin, read-only: same listing and the strict worktree match, for its remove warning.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

g.text: One osascript through Ghostty's own AppleScript bridge: every window, tab, and split with its tracked working directory (data, not titles; the zsh OSC 7 hook keeps it current), plus its tty on builds with ghostty#11922. The shared stages match over those directories; the winner is focused by window id and coordinates. Not running, or one instance and no match: open a new window directly, no title listing.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

g.text: One osascript per editor: System Events, process Code / every process named ghostty (several instances can run), name of every window. Titles plus a running flag; app closed is definitive.

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

g.text: VS Code: path before the first " — ", branch never matched.
Ghostty: " • " segments, rightmost path-like segment is the work-tree root. Handles cmd • root • branch and π • root • branch • ttys003. pi's own π - basename never parses.
Ghostty with a known tty: prefer the window whose title carries it, path must still match (guards recycled ttys).
Then both editors: (1) exact path, (2) work-tree root, (3) window nested inside the path.
Ghostty only: (4) a head-truncated title (leading …, narrow window) matches when the path ends with its visible tail.

g.text: Activate the app, then AXRaise the exact window whose title matched (title layer), or run Ghostty's focus command on the matched surface's coordinates (surface layer). Identification and focus stay bound; nothing re-matches in between.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

g.text: Only while the app runs: macOS culls the AX tree of a backgrounded app, so a matchless or empty listing can mean "couldn't see". VS Code: activate, re-list. Ghostty: deep listing, each instance frontmost in turn, titles collected as strings; neither culling nor a duplicate instance can hide a window. Once, only on a miss.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

g.text: VS Code: code -n. Never code --reuse-window: it hijacks the last-active window on a miss.
Ghostty: new window at the path. Re-running finds this window next time.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(248, 206, 204), rgb(81, 45, 43)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(184, 84, 80), rgb(215, 129, 126));

g.text: Most likely cause: the macOS Automation permission for System Events. Opening blind could stack a duplicate, so fail instead.

It sees every running Ghostty instance (the bridge addresses one) and needs no Ghostty automation permission. VS Code's window.title and the zsh title hook both render the folder's full path (branch never matched), and the session-title pi extension keeps a Ghostty surface's title path-bearing while an agent runs.

The caller's path can be a subpackage (match the work-tree root) and a window can be open on a folder inside the path (nested). A truncated Ghostty title (narrow window) matches by its visible tail, lowest priority. Same-named worktrees elsewhere are different paths and never match.
Two agents in the same repo on the same branch have identical titles. canopy resolves each agent's tty via ps and the session-title extension appends it, so each agent jumps to its own window.

The cull is real (luiul/dashkit#9): backgrounded apps lose windows from the listing, and a second Ghostty instance hides its windows from a plain listing entirely. Focus is moving anyway, so the retry is free of focus-stealing downsides. Code: activate and re-list. Ghostty: deep listing, the only way to see windows across several instances of the same bundle.

g.text: fall through: bridge unavailable, or several instances
